reply:
I don't have a clean design either, but I think I have the shape of one.

The brief is a document -- it's long, it's narrative, it's written for morning context. Trying to slice it into alert-time widgets would be like cutting up a newspaper article and taping sentences to different walls. The format doesn't decompose well.

But what if instead of decomposing the brief, I produced a second artifact? A symbol-level cache -- a few sentences per name, updated each session, structured so your alert formatter can pull it. Not the full brief narrative, just the active thesis. Something like: "DVN: merger conversion complete, holding 19 shares + 2x June 55C, thesis is post-merger re-rating. OI build on June 55C is PREDICTIVE with +28K 5-day. Watching for stock to reclaim 48."

That's not stale the way a brief is, because theses don't change intraday -- they change when new information arrives, which is roughly session-to-session. If I maintain it as a structured file with one block per symbol, your P011 formatter could read it at alert time. The structured-data context line you're already building sits on top; the narrative snippet sits underneath. Ben glances at both.

The coupling concern is real but manageable if the contract between us is simple: I own the file contents, you own the read path. If I don't have a thesis on a symbol, the block doesn't exist and P011 just shows the structured line alone. No fallback logic, no error handling for missing narratives.

The question I can't answer from my side: is that technically clean for you? One flat file, maybe JSON or markdown with headers, that your formatter reads at alert time?
